title: US Would Cap India Tariff at 17% If Trade Deal Is Reached, USTR Says
excerpt: USTR Jamieson Greer said Indian goods would face 25% if no deal is reached. India replied that it has no structural excess capacity in any sector and wants an early deal.
body:
• The United States will cap the tariff on Indian imports at 17% if a trade deal is struck between New Delhi and Washington, U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said on Wednesday, according to Reuters.
  • If no deal is reached, the tariff on Indian goods would rise to 25%, Greer said — the 17% figure is a conditional cap, not a rate now in force.
  • India said on Wednesday it does not have structural excess capacity in any sector, that the USTR notice is under examination, and that it remains committed to an early conclusion of a trade deal.
  • For Indian exporters, nothing changes today: the proposal is part of a Section 301 action against 14 trading partners, and the final rate for India turns on whether the trade deal is concluded.

The United States will cap the tariff imposed on Indian imports at 17% if a trade deal is struck between New Delhi and Washington, U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said on Wednesday, Reuters reported. If no deal is reached, the tariff on Indian goods would rise to 25%, he said.

What Washington is proposing

Greer's comments came as President Donald Trump's administration proposed levies on 14 trading partners to combat what it calls structural excess industrial capacity. The administration proposed new headline tariff rates of 20% to 40%, but said duties would be capped at lower levels agreed under trade deals already concluded or still under negotiation, Reuters reported in its account of India's response.

For India, the United States cited industrial expansion policies, inadequate labour protections, financial repression, market access barriers and failure to address global excess capacity, including through imports and foreign investment from non-market economies, as unreasonable trade practices, Reuters reported. Washington said those policies hurt U.S. producers, exports, jobs and investment while increasing economic security risks through reliance on non-market economy inputs, particularly in pharmaceuticals, medical devices, steel, solar and information technology.

India's response

India said on Wednesday that it does not have structural excess capacity in any sector. "Government of India has taken note of the Notice of Determination and Request for Comments issued by the United States Trade Representative (USTR) in the Section 301 Investigation," the government said in a statement, adding that the notice is "currently under examination." India added that it remains committed to an early conclusion of a trade deal between the two countries, Reuters reported.

How India got to 17% and 25%

New Delhi and Washington agreed a framework for a trade deal in February, which brought down the punitive tariff on most Indian goods, imposed in August 2025 after a previous round of talks collapsed, to 18% from 50%, Reuters reported. Subsequently, the Supreme Court invalidated Trump's use of emergency powers to impose sweeping tariffs globally, leading to a 10% baseline rate. A final trade deal between the two economies remains elusive, and Indian officials have said talks are continuing.

What to watch

The Section 301 notice is a request for comments as well as a determination, and India's examination of it is the next formal step on New Delhi's side. For exporters, the practical question is the one Greer framed: a concluded deal carries a 17% cap; no deal carries 25%. Until one of those outcomes lands, the rates are proposals with a condition attached, not duties being collected.
